court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Suraj Khushalsingh Rajput And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Maharashtra And Another (state)

facts_of_case: Parties have arrived at amicable settlement. Accused seeking quashing of FIR and proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
legal_principles.held: The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303

legal_principles.principle: The High Court must have due regard to the facts and circumstances of each case before exercising its power to quash a criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R.
